name: Community Nature Fund
summary: Small grants for community projects that create, improve or expand space for wildlife inside the Peak District National Park, such as wildflower meadows, hedgerows, ponds and bird or bat boxes.
reporting: Grantees submit a simple evaluation form on the difference the project made, and must maintain anything bought or built with the grant for at least 5 years.

eligibility.rule: The project site is not already managed or protected for nature
A previous Community Nature Fund grant is fully spent and evaluated before reapplying
Owns the project land or has the landowner's permission before applying
For an individual landowner, the project is not-for-profit and shows clear benefits for nature
The project has no general running costs, pre-award work, recoverable VAT or statutory-duty costs

documents: Site map or plan showing the project layout and activities

amount.quote: Grants of between £500 and £5,000 are available towards the specific costs of delivering your project

reporting.quote: You will be asked to submit a simple evaluation form to tell us about the difference that your project has made You will be responsible for maintaining anything bought or built with your grant for a minimum of 5 years

effort.quote: Download an application form, fill in and return to us at hello@peakdistrictfoundation.org.uk

eligibility.quote: We cannot fund projects taking place on sites which are already managed or protected for nature (e.g. Sites of Special Scientific Interest, Local/National Nature Reserves).
If you have received a Community Nature Fund grant before, then you will need to have finished spending it and returned a completed evaluation form before you can apply for another grant.
If you do not own the land on which the project will take place, then you must ensure that you have the landowner's permission to carry out the project before you apply.
Individual landowners (as long as the project you are applying for is not-for-profit and you can show clear benefits for nature)

• your general running costs (e.g. overheads, core staff salaries) • any work which takes place before your grant is awarded • recoverable VAT • the costs of fulfilling a statutory duty, obligation or planning consent

after_award.quote: to complete and return a simple evaluation form within 12 months of receiving your grant, to tell us about the difference it has made

documents.quote: When you send us your completed form, please include a map / plan which shows the rough layout of the site and where the specific activities involved in your project will take place
